uncited: It is distinct from [Ambient Occlusion via SDF](1631-ambient-occlusion-via-sdf.md) as it relies on view-dependent distance rather than local geometric curvature, and from [Multi-Layer Shading / OmniShader](2511-multi-layer-shading-omnishader.md) by being a post-compositing or per-sample color modulation rather than a complex multi-pass lighting integration.
No specific complex data structures are required beyond the standard ray-marching state (current position, accumulated color, step size).
The fractional depth $d_v$ is maintained as a scalar accumulator.
**Calculate Fractional Depth:** Determine the total length of the ray segment traversing the volume ($L_{total}$) and the current distance traveled from the camera origin ($L_{current}$).
**Output:** Use $c_d$ as the color contribution for the current sample in the volume integration loop.
If $c_b$ is a shade of gray ($a, a, a$), only intensity depth-cuing (dimming) occurs.

Unlike simple intensity depth-cuing which only reduces brightness, this method modulates the color spectrum (typically adding blue) to exploit the human visual tendency for cool colors to recede [S2][S7, unofficial].

The claim states that the method modulates the color spectrum (typically adding blue) to exploit the tendency for cool colors to recede, unlike simple intensity depth-cuing which only reduces brightness. Source [S7] explicitly states that the technique augments standard intensity depth-cuing with color modulation, increasing the amount of blue in distant samples to simulate aerial perspective. It further explains that this exploits the tendency of cool colors (such as blue) to recede visually. Source [S2] corroborates this by describing a technique that dims voxels (intensity) and adds a blue hue (color spectrum modulation) to distant voxels, relying on the tendency for cool colors to fade into the background. Both sources confirm that simple intensity depth-cuing involves dimming, while the described method adds blue color modulation to enhance depth perception based on color recession.
